# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Denial of Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702) — Reference Number POC-E14E3A00BC-47205**
**Member: Quinn Iverson | Member ID: W154693844 | Date of Notice: 2026-08-14**
**Governing Policy: Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf**

Dear Wellpoint Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my total ankle replacement surgery (CPT 27702), which was denied on 2026-08-14 for the stated reason that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe my records show that I meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## Why I believe my records meet the plan's criteria

The Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery state that ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary when several conditions are met, including:

> "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved"

My records address the first two of these directly:

- **Radiographic confirmation:** Weight-bearing ankle radiographs from 2026-07-17 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.
- **Conservative management exceeding 3 months:** I completed 16 weeks (2026-03-24 to 2026-07-14) of supervised physical therapy — 20 visits — focused on ankle strengthening and balance, along with 4 months of NSAIDs and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-05 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This is well beyond the plan's 3-month threshold, and it did not resolve my pain or restore my function. I continue to walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks, with exam findings of positive provocative testing and painful, limited range of motion.

The remaining two elements of this criterion — vascular perfusion status and FDA approval of the device — are not addressed in the materials I have seen. I am asking my surgeon's office to supply [documentation of lower extremity vascular perfusion, e.g., pedal pulse findings] and [confirmation that the device to be used is FDA approved] to complete the record on these points.

The guideline also describes the conservative management that should be attempted:

> "Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:"

and

> "• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My records show more than one of the listed complementary strategies: structured activity modification through 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 4 months of anti-inflammatory medication, and a corticosteroid injection. I am also asking my surgeon's office to confirm whether footwear modification or a padding/accommodative device such as a foot orthosis was tried or discussed, since I do not see that specifically documented, and to add [footwear modification/orthotic documentation, if applicable] to the file if it exists.

Given the length and extent of the conservative treatment I completed, and the imaging showing advanced joint deterioration, I do not believe the reason given for this denial — that my conservative care trial was inadequate — is supported by my own chart.

## What I am asking

I am asking Wellpoint to reconsider this denial in light of the policy language above and the corresponding documentation in my medical record, and to approve the requested total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). If any additional records — such as vascular exam findings, device FDA status, or footwear/orthotic history — would help complete this review, please let me know specifically what is needed so my surgeon's office can provide it.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-10, and I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial notice, consistent with Wellpoint's instructions to use the address on the notice itself.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

[Quinn Iverson]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W154693844
Date: [date of submission]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.policy_title: Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon)
quotes: • Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved Total ankle arthroplasty may also be indicated for revision of failed previous reconstructions where sufficient bone stock and soft tissue integrity are present.
If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented.

Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:

• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate.
If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approa ch is not reasonable.
Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended.

Log in at anthem.com or call the number on your card, and send your written appeal to the address on your denial letter. Online: anthem.com, or the Sydney Health app By phone: The number on the back of your ID card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative.
